answer: Because the pearl calculation reruns each epoch, the marble weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the nebula settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 90 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 26% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 17 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
